title: Kentucky needs last-gasp 3-pointer to avoid upset vs. 30.5-point underdog
content:
Kentucky defeated Northern Arizona 78-77 at Rupp Arena on Friday night. The No. 24 Wildcats entered the game as a 3o.5-point favorite and needed a 3-pointer from transfer guard Alex Wilkins with 2.1 seconds remaining to win.

Kentucky entered the game ranked No. 36 in KenPom. Northern Arizona was No. 299 out of 365 Division I teams. The Lumberjacks went 10-22 last season, including a 4-14, last-place finish in the Big Sky. NAU was picked to finish last again in the Big Sky this preseason.

“I (thought) our defensive energy was good,” Kentucky coach Mark Pope said after the win. “I thought our defensive execution was incredibly poor.

“I hope everybody at Rupp (Arena) had fun,” Pope added. “It was a pretty exciting game. You saw a Northern Arizona team that is playing great basketball and a Kentucky team that’s trying to find themselves; it came down to the last second. It was pretty entertaining; if not well-executed, it was really entertaining, and I think (Northern Arizona) will be a fun team to follow.”

Northern Arizona (0-4) held a four-point lead with 22 seconds left, but Kentucky answered with a made jumper, and NAU followed by missing a pair of free throws on the front end of 1-and-1s. The second miss led to Wilkins’ game-winning 3-pointer. Officials reviewed Wilkins’ shot to see if his foot was on the line, but referees upheld the 3-pointer. A last-gasp halfcourt heave by NAU clanked off the backboard.

Those were Northern Arizona’s only missed free throws, and the Lumberjacks finished the game shooting 10-for-12 from the stripe. Wilkins finished with 14 points, tied with two teammates for the team high. NAU’s Chris Komin led all scorers with 25 points.

UK’s last regular-season loss to a mid-major opponent came against UNC Wilmington (No. 119 KenPom) in December 2023 — the same season the Wildcats lost to Oakland (No. 131) in the opening round of the NCAA Tournament as a No. 3 seed. A loss Friday would have been Kentucky’s worst by KenPom rankings since falling to Evansville (No. 294) in November 2019.

Kentucky (3-1) lost to Kansas by 20 in the Champions Classic Tuesday night at the United Center in Chicago. The Wildcats are coming off a 22-14 season in 2025-26 in which they reached the NCAA Tournament as a 7-seed and lost in the second round. The finish stirred some disappointment with a passionate Kentucky fanbase that was frustrated with the campaign despite a $22 million roster budget, believed to be the highest in the sport. Pope is a beloved former Kentucky player and part of the 1995-96 “Untouchables” national championship team coached by Rick Pitino, but this week’s results won’t help calm the waters in Lexington.
